description: Labels of the JavaScript and TypeScript candidates of the v0.3 exports of 84 npm sources that are not known vulnerable sites. Criteria: PROTOCOL.md.
assigned_by: AI coding assistant (Claude), reading the package source
reviewed_by: project owner, 2026-11-15: 31 of 78 labels, namely every label the assistant had assigned safe or undetermined
review_note: Reviewed interactively with the code excerpt of each item. 12 labels changed (_thi.ng__egf_0.3.0|lib/index.umd.js|None; git-parse_1.0.4|dist/checkout_commit.js|None; git-parse_1.0.4|dist/git_diff.js|None; git-parse_1.0.4|dist/git_log_stream.js|None; git-parse_1.0.4|dist/git_pull.js|None; launch-editor_2.14.1|index.js|167; launch-editor_2.14.1|index.js|172; monorepo-build_0.1.9|lib/index.test.js|12; nodemon_3.1.14|lib/monitor/run.js|430; nodemon_3.1.14|lib/monitor/run.js|434; react-dev-utils_11.0.0|openBrowser.js|92; roar-pidusage_1.1.6|lib/helpers.js|12). The reviewer labels an alert on a require line by the command calls of that module. The 47 labels the assistant assigned vulnerable have review null: not reviewed by a person. CVE identifiers in the notes are the reviewer's statements.

labels.label: safe
labels.reason: Each `pid` is `+blocks[1]`, a number parsed from the `lsof` output; non-numeric values are dropped.

review.note: SAFE - Numeric validation. The PID is converted to a number using unary +, and invalid numeric values are rejected before execution. Therefore, shell metacharacters cannot be injected through pid into exec('kill ' + pid). However, the same module contains a separate confirmed command injection vulnerability at line 9 (CVE-2021-23360), where the unvalidated port parameter is interpolated into a shell command.

labels.label: vulnerable
labels.reason: On Windows the editor and file name go to cmd.exe after `^` escaping written for this package; its strength cannot be judged from the code.

review.note: VULNERABLE - Confirmed OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-112943). The Windows branch constructs a shell command using custom caret-based escaping, but escapeCmdArgs() fails to neutralize % characters. Windows CMD environment-variable expansion can bypass the intended escaping and introduce executable shell syntax. The vulnerability affects launch-editor 2.14.1 and was fixed in 2.14.2. Classified as a confirmed true positive.

labels.label: vulnerable
labels.reason: `spawn(editor, args)` uses no shell, but the program name comes from the caller, the environment or the process list.

review.note: VULNERABLE - Confirmed Argument Injection (CVE-2026-112944, CWE-88). Although spawn() executes without a shell, the application forwards potentially attacker-controlled filenames directly to editor CLI arguments. Filenames beginning with '+' or '-' may be interpreted as executable commands or options by editors such as Vim and Emacs. The vulnerability affects launch-editor 2.14.1 and was fixed in 2.14.2.

labels.label: undetermined

review.note: UNCERTAIN - Build-tool process execution. The spawn() wrapper executes build tools using command, arguments, and options supplied by internal callers. Shell execution is disabled by default but may be enabled through opts.shell. The wrapper performs no local validation. Execution is an intended feature of node-gyp, and no concrete attacker-controlled injection path has been established. Further analysis of internal call sites, configuration sources, and shell options is required.

labels.label: safe

review.note: SAFE - Sanitized shell command. The notifier executable is escaped using shellwords.escape(). Arguments are constructed through constructArgumentList() with an allowlist of option names, recursive escaping of array elements, escaping of shell-sensitive characters, and double-quote wrapping. No effective command injection path was identified through the reviewed notifysend.js caller. The CodeQL finding is classified as a false positive for OS Command Injection.

review.note: SAFE - OS-generated process identifier. The command uses a fixed taskkill structure, with child.pid obtained from a child process created by nodemon. The PID is generated by the operating system and is numeric, so shell metacharacters cannot enter the command through the identified data flow. No command injection vulnerability is established at this execution site.

labels.label: safe

Before reaching either exec() call, child.kill(signal) validates the signal through Node.js. Invalid signal strings containing shell metacharacters are rejected, preventing their propagation to the shell commands. No exploitable OS Command Injection path is identified through the reviewed inputs.

review.note: VULNERABLE - OS Command Injection. The exported openBrowser() function passes a caller-controlled URL through encodeURI() into a shell command executed by execSync() on macOS. encodeURI() preserves $, ( and ), allowing shell command substitution inside double quotes. The vulnerable execution pattern is documented in CVE-2026-14802. Although normal development-server URLs may be trusted, the exported API permits crafted input to reach the execution sink.

review.note: UNCERTAIN - Windows CMD execution with environment-derived editor. The function invokes cmd.exe /C with an editor and arguments potentially sourced from environment variables. The filename is restricted by a Windows-specific allowlist, but editor configuration and initial arguments are not subject to equivalent validation. shellQuote.parse() does not guarantee Windows CMD escaping. No confirmed attacker-controlled injection path has been established. Exploitability depends on configuration trust boundaries.

labels.label: undetermined

The Windows-specific branch concatenates npm/yarn/pnpm command arguments using command.join(' ') and executes the resulting string with shell: true, without argument escaping. Configurable values such as tag, publishArgs, and versionArgs may introduce shell metacharacters. However, no concrete attacker-controlled input path has been established. Exploitability depends on the trustworthiness and validation of upstream arguments.

labels.label: vulnerable
labels.reason: Both callers of `getconf` in the package pass the literals 'CLK_TCK' and 'PAGESIZE'.

review.note: VULNERABLE - OS Command Injection. The exported getconf() function concatenates its keyword parameter directly into a shell command executed via child_process.exec(), without validation or escaping. Although both internal callers pass constant values (CLK_TCK and PAGESIZE), external consumers can invoke the exported function with attacker-controlled input. Shell metacharacters can therefore reach the execution sink.

No specific attacker-controlled injection path has been established. Exploitability depends on whether consuming applications incorporate untrusted input into command strings without appropriate sanitization.
